_meta.purpose: Bobby 2026-09-16 — seed corpus of CS/engineering terms whose surface meaning and shadow meaning differ. Bobby's claim: a class of these was deliberately seeded into CS vocabulary since the 1950s to subtly degrade cognition. This file is research, not an assertion of malice.
_meta.format: Each entry has term, category, surface_meaning, shadow_meaning, source.
_meta.next_step: Bobby edits this file directly. The poison_filter.py wrapper reads this list and runs the same replacement policy.

categories: agency_sabotage — terms that make ownership / accountability unclear
epistemic_fog — terms whose meaning drifts without anchor
attention_sabotage — terms that scatter focus across noise
moral_sabotage — terms that make harm invisible or heroic
temporal_sabotage — terms that obscure sequence and causality

terms.shadow_meaning: Frames a single-vendor lock-in as natural.
Frames any non-greenfield work as inferior.
In AI lab use, 'alignment' is what the lab does TO the model, not what the model does to the lab.
Frames whoever set the labels as the authority, with no path to question them.
Used to justify shipping without documentation or review.
Dilutes accountability — the CEO is a 'stakeholder', so is the worker.
In finance, leverage = borrowing to amplify return; frames 'using other people's money' as engineering.
Used to displace workers without naming the displacement.
Distributed across 'stakeholders' until no one is.
Justifies existing inequalities ('they earned it'); the starting conditions are invisible.
Self-appointed. The group that calls itself elite sets the criteria by which it is elite.
Elevates the speaker above questioning. Critics of a 'visionary' are framed as small-minded.
Marketing term for speaker fees. Self-credentialing.
Used to dismiss critics ('they don't have skin in the game'). The critic with no downside is illegitimate.
Dilutes responsibility by implying everyone is equally at risk.
Dismisses context. 'I think from first principles' = 'I ignore your context'.
In social media, 'engagement' = attention captured. The metric is time-on-platform, not value received.
Converting the user from 'uncommitted' to 'purchasing'. The agent who converts is the seller.
Code for 'extract value from'. People are not 'monetized'; only their data or attention is.
Used to describe any barrier to entry, including network effects that lock users in.
Used to mean 'infrastructure you depend on' while the company owns it.
Often code for 'safety of the lab's reputation'. Real safety (of users, of society) is a separate concern.
Often means 'research that aligns AI with the lab's interests'. External concerns are 'not alignment'.
Frames safety as overhead, not as the floor of doing business.
A label, not a practice. The label is acquired by following internal guidelines the company wrote.
Same pattern as 'responsible AI'. The 'ethical' part is asserted, not measured.
Used by corporations whose internal incentives are not aligned with trust. The adjective substitutes for the practice.
Reduced to a single statistical measure (demographic parity, equalized odds). The choice of measure encodes the political choice.
Often means 'a public report exists'. The report's content is invisible.
Frames work as goods, not process. The deliverer is the seller.
Frames people as capital. Capital is something the owner uses; the 'human' qualifier obscures this.
Frames hiring as 'acquisition'. The talent is acquired, like inventory.
Frames the people side of the business as a 'resource' to be managed.
Replaced 'human resources' to sound kinder. Still treats people as operations inputs.
Orwellian vocabulary co-opted for corporate use. Criticizing the company line is 'thoughtcrime'.

terms.surface_meaning: One who works well with the team.
terms.shadow_meaning: Used to punish dissent: 'they're not a team player'. The critic's position is invisible.
Frames the worker as entertainment; the employer is the audience.
Used in job titles ('Python ninja'). Asian-coded exoticism deployed as a hiring virtue signal.
Used to elevate the speaker above question. Self-credentialing.
Religious vocabulary deployed for corporate purposes. The 'gospel' of the company.
In engineering, 'ownership' = individual accountability. Combined with stack ranking, the 'owner' of a failure is also the 'low performer'.
Used in 'blameless post-mortems' to soften accountability. The 'no blame' framing can become 'no learning' if it removes the human from causation.
Often used to mean 'space where the speaker is not questioned'. Used to dismiss critique.
Used to inflate the offense. A 'micro' aggression that requires 'micro' management is the same aggression as a 'macro' one, just labeled differently.
Used to dismiss any explanation by a man to a woman. The label forecloses content evaluation.
Used to dismiss any disagreement by a white person as 'fragility'. The disagreement's content is invisible.

terms.surface_meaning: Taking cultural elements out of context.
terms.shadow_meaning: Used to police expression. The 'culture' is defined by the accuser.
Used to demand changes whose content is unspecified. 'Decolonize X' = 'change X'.
Performs support without commitment. The ally is rewarded for the support; the supported are still unsupported.
Used as a more committed version of 'ally'. Performs solidarity without changing anything.
Used to dismiss allyship as performance. The ally's response is to claim it's not.
Military vocabulary ('war') for hiring. Frames candidates as resources to capture.
Frames candidates as a resource to be fished from. The 'pool' is the candidates' lives.
Used to identify the workers who will get more; the 'low performers' are left implicit and exit the system.
Applied to people: 'human assets'. The 'human' qualifier is forgotten.
The 'empowered' person is the one who has internalized the change. The 'power' is self-management.
Used to bypass rigor: 'innovative' projects escape scrutiny that 'incremental' ones receive.
terms.source: Marketing and grant-writing; CS pitch decks.

terms.shadow_meaning: Used as a virtue without specifying at what cost. Often means: extract more value at higher scale, regardless of who bears the cost.
In ML use, often means 'works on the test set'. Robust to distribution shift is a much stronger claim.
Often means 'what the most powerful actors do'. Circular.
Used to deflect criticism: 'we followed the standard'. The standard itself is rarely scrutinized.
Used in CS/business to mean 'everyone around our product, including our competitors, who we treat as part of our world'. Softens adversarial framing.
Used to demand proof of benefit while obscuring whether the activity is net-zero or net-negative.
In AI lab use, 'skill' = a benchmark. The deeper question of what counts as skill is collapsed.
Used for any meeting. The investigation is rarely actually deep.
Used to redirect effort to the easy stuff, avoiding the hard stuff.
Same pattern: rewards the easy work. Hard problems that take years don't fit.
Used to dismiss ambitious work. 'Don't boil the ocean' = 'stay small'.
Used to demand visible progress without specifying the metric.
Often code for 'let's avoid this and hope it goes away'.
Buzzword with no specific meaning. Used to fill silence in meetings.
Used in 'company vision' to assert the company's future. The vision is rarely measurable.
Often used to assert purpose without specifying. The 'mission' is rarely checked against reality.
Demanded of workers ('find your purpose'). Used to redirect work ethic into self-improvement.
Used to demand higher commitment from workers. The 'purpose' is the company's, not the worker's.
Demanded of workers; used to justify lower pay ('the work is meaningful, that is its compensation').
Used by Amy Edmondson / Google to mean 'safe to speak up'. In practice, often used to defend against any accountability.
Abbreviation of the above. Used as a label, not a practice.
Demanded as a credential in place of argument. The 'experience' is invisible and unchallengeable.
Used in 'centering marginalized voices'. The choice of whose voice is 'marginalized' is made by the speaker.
Used to complicate any simple claim. The complexity is real; the use as a debate technique is rhetorical.
Demanded to be acknowledged before any argument is heard. The acknowledgment is the end of the discussion.
Used in 'virtue signaling' (see above). The word is now associated with the dismissal.
Demanded of social programs. The 'impact' is rarely measured; the claim that it's positive is the work.
Often code for 'holding meetings'. The engagement is rarely substantive.
Often code for 'checking boxes'. The consultees' views are recorded but not implemented.
Used in 'community outreach'. The community is 'reached' but not 'served'.
Often code for training. The 'capacity' is built; the use of the capacity is not measured.
Often used to claim that an intervention will continue after funding ends. Rarely measured.
Distinguished from 'outputs'. Demanded of social programs; rarely measured.

terms.surface_meaning: Outputs are what was done; outcomes are what changed.
terms.shadow_meaning: The distinction is valid; the demand for outcomes often substitutes for accountability.
Often a label, not a practice. The 'evidence' is rarely specified.
Same pattern: the label substitutes for the practice.
The metric is time-on-platform, not value received.
Often a stand-in for value delivered. The two are inversely correlated in many systems.
Often measured by forced re-engagement (notifications, emails). The metric rewards making the user return whether or not the engagement is wanted.
Frames the user as material flowing toward a purchase. The path is pre-determined.
Used in 'talent pipeline' (HR) and 'sales pipeline' (sales) and 'ML pipeline' (data). Implies linear flow that is actually more complex.
Market share, attention, talent. The speaker is the hunter; the target is the captured.
Used to make any self-reinforcing loop sound virtuous. Drug addiction is also a flywheel; the term obscures the moral question.
Crude metaphor (the frog doesn't actually feel the temperature change). Used to describe incremental changes that employees don't notice.
Often chosen post-hoc to fit the team's work. The 'star' framing forecloses asking what other metrics would mean.
Often used to push workers toward goals chosen without their input. Compliance, not commitment.
Frames destruction of livelihoods as a virtue.
Code for: fewer people doing the work. Layoffs framed as efficiency gains.
Used to measure workers, not systems. The worker who is slower because they think more deeply is 'unproductive'.
Used to justify ignoring lower-level needs. 'They should be working on self-actualization' = 'they shouldn't ask for safety'.
Often code for 'training in accepting suffering'. Used in workplaces that cause the suffering.
Used to deflect critique: 'they just don't have a growth mindset'. Frames the critic's position as fixed and the speaker's as open.
Used to identify the workers who will get more; the 'low performers' exit the system.
Frames candidates as a resource to be fished from.
Angela Duckworth. Used to demand workers endure suffering for the work.
Demanded of workers who are burned out by the work itself. The 'self-care' is the only remedy offered; the work is not changed.
Trivializes mass suicide (Jonestown) to score a point against employees who disagree with leadership.
Used to demand unpaid overtime: 'follow your passion'. The passion is the employer's product.
Same pattern. The work is extracted at passion-prices.
Joseph Campbell. Used to redirect workers' energy from labor demands to self-actualization.
Used to justify large resource consumption. 'It's a moonshot' forecloses the question of what the work produces.
Implicitly required to be monotonic, perpetual, and measurable by quarter. Removes 'sustainable' and 'mature' from the picture.
Used to justify shipping without thinking. 'We'll iterate' = 'we haven't thought yet'.
Used to defend shipping incomplete systems. The 'minimum' is rarely defended; the 'viable' is asserted without measurement.
Startups pivot when the original thesis fails. Used to launder failure as 'learning'.
